A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hyper-GCN work. Full inspection covers their text, equations, figures, tables and references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original recognition results on NTU-60, NTU-120 and NW-UCLA, component ablations, learned-feature visualizations and model-complexity measurements.

after.justification: v3 reports original base/large Hyper-GCN benchmark results in Table 1, component ablations in Tables 2–3 and learned-feature analyses in Figures 4–6.

M1.justification: Equations (6)–(7) replace symmetric hyper-graph normalization with left degree normalization and squared Euclidean distance with Euclidean distance before softmax. These change the reported aggregation and connection weighting within the retained architecture. The base/large model widths match v2's lightweight/standard configurations.

E1.justification: Both versions use NTU-60, NTU-120 and NW-UCLA for skeleton-based action recognition, with the same named evaluation splits and four illustrated action categories. Additional model-size results remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated comparisons with ST-GCN, 2s-AGCN, DC-GCN+ADG and MS-G3D. DSTA-Net, IIP-Transformer and SkateFormer previously appeared only in the NTU-120 complexity comparison; v3 also compares them on NTU-60, and SkateFormer on NW-UCLA. This substantially broadens the competitors assessed on retained benchmarks.

E3.justification: v3 extends reported evaluation of the retained lightweight/base configuration from NTU-120 to NTU-60 and NW-UCLA. Added ST-GCN and 2s-AGCN comparisons use J+B inputs, introducing two-stream comparisons alongside four-stream methods. Existing splits, optimizer settings and the 140-epoch schedule remain unchanged. Identifying the ablations as using the base model is newly disclosed information.

E4.justification: The existing Figure 4 case study is revised, including the selected joint groups reported for standing up and kicking. The K sweep, hyper-joint-count/divergence-loss ablation, cosine matrices and t-SNE analysis are retained; no new robustness test or ablation question is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. Recognition results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Standard/large four-stream NTU-120 results change from 90.5/91.7 to 90.9/92.0, and NW-UCLA from 97.1 to 97.6; NTU-60 scores also change. Matching lightweight/base NTU-120 scores change from 90.4/91.5 to 90.5/91.7, with additional benchmark entries. The single-stream row is removed. Table III/3 changes the five-hyper-joint result with divergence loss from 84.8 to 86.8. Newly included SkateFormer results show 98.3 on NW-UCLA, above Hyper-GCN's 97.6. These are reported revisions, without an established explanation for the score changes.

T1.justification: Equation (6) changes D_v^(-1/2) H W D_e^(-1) H^T D_v^(-1/2) to D_v^(-1) H W D_e^(-1) H^T, and Equation (7) removes the squared distance. These are non-equivalent mathematical definitions. Other mathematical development is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The same three contributions—adaptive non-uniform hyper-graphs, virtual joints and Hyper-GCN—and the broad state-of-the-art claim on three datasets remain in the introduction and conclusion. Dropping the abstract's specific NTU-120 accuracy sentence does not redefine the core contribution or claimed task scope.

C2.justification: The kicking explanation changes to left-leg motion relative to the extended right hand, correcting inconsistent earlier limb descriptions. Standing is explained through fixed hand and foot joints instead of a stationary right foot alone. Section 4.3 also distinguishes base/large performance and explicitly reports second place on one benchmark. Existing noise and redundant-hyper-joint explanations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link, explicitly states that hyper-joints are shared across frames, and identifies the base configuration used for ablations. These improve documentation without establishing that those implementation choices changed. Hardware and training hyperparameters are retained; repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v3 adds works on metaverse/synthetic data, recurrent-attention pose prediction and visual-semantic gesture recognition. It removes the anomaly-detection survey, Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks citation and unused trailing references. The positioning against fixed hyper-graphs and pairwise GCN/Transformer topology remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local revisions update the abstract ending, clarify architecture terminology, consolidate the separate complexity subsection into architecture/comparison passages, and add author contact information and acknowledgments. This is limited editing rather than extensive narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: The document template changes throughout, including abstract placement, headings, captions and float positions. Table 1 consolidates v2's Tables I and IV, adds resource columns and expands method groupings. Figure 2 explicitly depicts virtual-joint propagation/removal and corrects module labels. Figure 4 is redrawn with joint-membership highlighting instead of the previous joint-size weight encoding.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline/resource comparisons, clearer implementation disclosure and a code-access link make v3 easier to assess. Correcting the 84.8 ablation entry to 86.8 also resolves a demonstrable inconsistency. These reporting gains outweigh the limited loss of single-stream benchmark visibility, although unexplained changes to the mathematical operators and main accuracies limit the overall improvement.
